question: You are at a social gathering and notice two groups of people. One is a group of strangers and is having an interesting conversation that you would like to join, while the other group includes someone you know well. What do you do next?
answer:

The thought of inserting myself into that conversation makes me anxious. What if they think I'm intruding? What if I say something stupid and embarrass myself?

And yet, the other group is someone I know well... but do I really want to go over there? That person can be so draining sometimes. They always seem to dominate the conversation and make me feel like I'm just a listener, not an equal participant.

I think I would probably end up doing nothing. Just standing there, observing both groups, hoping no one notices me. It's easier that way. At least then I don't have to deal with the pressure of making small talk or trying to fit in.

But deep down, I know this isn't really an option. Eventually, someone will notice me just standing there and might come over to chat. Or worse, my friend from the other group will come looking for me and expect me to join them. Ugh, why can't I just be left alone?!

I guess I'll just have to muster up some fake enthusiasm and pretend to be interested in whatever conversation is happening. Maybe then I can sneak back into my comfort zone and observe from a safe distance. Sigh... social gatherings are just so exhausting.
